\/\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cbr class=\"Apple-interchange-newline\" style=\"-webkit-text-size-adjust: auto;\" \/\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EHydroxychloroquine in SLE\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"-webkit-text-size-adjust: 100%; background-color: white; font-family: \u0026quot;Times New Roman\u0026quot;, serif; font-size: 18.66666603088379px;\"\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"-webkit-text-size-adjust: 100%; background-color: white; font-family: \u0026quot;Times New Roman\u0026quot;, serif; font-size: 18.66666603088379px;\"\u003E“Chloroquine, together with its hydroxyl derivative hydroxychloroquine, was initially used as an antimalarial agent, but is also useful in the treatment of autoimmune diseases such as rheumatoid arthritis and systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE).\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"-webkit-text-size-adjust: 100%; background-color: white; font-family: \u0026quot;Times New Roman\u0026quot;, serif; font-size: 18.66666603088379px;\"\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"-webkit-text-size-adjust: 100%; background-color: white; font-family: \u0026quot;Times New Roman\u0026quot;, serif; font-size: 18.66666603088379px;\"\u003EChloroquine and hydroxychloroquine are approved for the treatment of SLE and have been shown to reduce the frequency of disease flares (particularly of lupus nephritis),\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/span\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"-webkit-text-size-adjust: 100%; background-color: white; font-family: \u0026quot;Times New Roman\u0026quot;, serif; font-size: 18.66666603088379px;\"\u003Econtribute to the maintenance of remission, prolong the onset of disease and reduce the risk of complications.\u003C\/span\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"-webkit-text-size-adjust: 100%; background-color: white; font-family: \u0026quot;Times New Roman\u0026quot;, serif; font-size: 18.66666603088379px;\"\u003EBeyond their immunomodulatory effects in SLE, these agents have also been shown to protect against thrombotic events,\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/span\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"-webkit-text-size-adjust: 100%; background-color: white; font-family: \u0026quot;Times New Roman\u0026quot;, serif; font-size: 18.66666603088379px;\"\u003Eimprove glucose and lipid profiles, and prevent renal damage,\u003C\/span\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"-webkit-text-size-adjust: 100%; background-color: white; font-family: \u0026quot;Times New Roman\u0026quot;, serif; font-size: 18.66666603088379px;\"\u003Eapparently resulting in reduced cardiovascular risk, for which SLE is an independent risk factor”\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003ESource:\u0026nbsp;\u003Ca href=\"https:\/\/www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov\/pmc\/articles\/PMC7097534\/\"\u003Ehttps:\/\/www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov\/pmc\/articles\/PMC7097534\/\u003C\/a\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cp\u003ESulfasalazine:\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EImmunosuppressive drug used in the treatment of cutaneous manifestations of lupus.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp style=\"-webkit-tap-highlight-color: rgba(0, 0, 0, 0); -webkit-text-size-adjust: 100%; box-sizing: border-box; color: #333333; font-family: \u0026quot;fira sans\u0026quot;, Arial, \u0026quot;helvetica neue\u0026quot;, Helvetica, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; margin: 0px 0px 10px;\"\u003E\u003Cspan class=\"ej-keyword\" data-value=\"Sulfasalazine\" style=\"box-sizing: inherit;\"\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp style=\"-webkit-tap-highlight-color: rgba(0, 0, 0, 0); -webkit-text-size-adjust: 100%; box-sizing: border-box; color: #333333; font-family: \u0026quot;fira sans\u0026quot;, Arial, \u0026quot;helvetica neue\u0026quot;, Helvetica, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; margin: 0px 0px 10px;\"\u003E\u003Cspan class=\"ej-keyword\" data-value=\"Sulfasalazine\" style=\"box-sizing: inherit;\"\u003E“Sulfasalazine\u003C\/span\u003E\u0026nbsp;is an effective agent for\u0026nbsp;\u003Cspan class=\"ej-keyword\" data-value=\"chronic discoid lupus erythematosus\" style=\"box-sizing: inherit;\"\u003Echronic discoid lupus erythematosus\u003C\/span\u003E\u0026nbsp;(CDLE) but the response to treatment is considerably variable between patients and is also unpredictable. The reason for this might relate to differences in metabolism of the drug which is extensively acetylated by the polymorphic enzyme N-acetyltransferase 2 (\u003Cspan class=\"ej-keyword\" data-value=\"NAT2\" style=\"box-sizing: inherit;\"\u003ENAT2\u003C\/span\u003E). To test this possibility, the N-acetylation phenotype of eleven patients with CDLE and treated by standard doses of\u0026nbsp;\u003Cspan class=\"ej-keyword\" data-value=\"sulfasalazine\" style=\"box-sizing: inherit;\"\u003Esulfasalazine\u003C\/span\u003E\u0026nbsp;was retrospectively determined by genotyping. A clear-cut difference in the outcome of treatment was observed according to whether the patients were slow acetylators (SA) or rapid acetylators (RA). Eight out of 11 patients responded to treatment with a complete or marked remission of the disease. Seven of them were RA. The three other patients who did not respond at all to the drug were SA. In addition, SA seem to be more prone to toxic events. These findings strongly suggest that the genetic polymorphism of\u0026nbsp;\u003Cspan class=\"ej-keyword\" data-value=\"NAT2\" style=\"box-sizing: inherit;\"\u003ENAT2\u003C\/span\u003E\u0026nbsp;is responsible for differences in the response to\u0026nbsp;\u003Cspan class=\"ej-keyword\" data-value=\"sulfasalazine\" style=\"box-sizing: inherit;\"\u003Esulfasalazine\u003C\/span\u003E\u0026nbsp;in patients with CDLE. Therefore, candidates for\u0026nbsp;\u003Cspan class=\"ej-keyword\" data-value=\"sulfasalazine\" style=\"box-sizing: inherit;\"\u003Esulfasalazine\u003C\/span\u003E\u0026nbsp;therapy should be genotyped to identify those patients who might benefit from the drug.”\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ESource:\u0026nbsp;\u003Ca href=\"https:\/\/journals.lww.com\/jpharmacogenetics\/Abstract\/1997\/04000\/NAT2_genotyping_and_efficacy_of_sulfasalazine_in.6.aspx\"\u003Ehttps:\/\/journals.lww.com\/jpharmacogenetics\/Abstract\/1997\/04000\/NAT2_genotyping_and_efficacy_of_sulfasalazine_in.6.aspx\u003C\/a\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EMethyl prednisolone: Glucocorticoids (GCs) are the mainstay of treatment of SLE as induction therapy and to manage acute flares and have dramatically improved the prognosis of severe SLE.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EIntravenous (IV) pulse methylprednisolone therapy, mostly 500-1,000 mg daily for 1-3 days, was introduced in the 1970s (Cathcart, 1976) and is remarkably efficacious in critically ill patients (Isenberg, 1982), suffering renal impairment, central nervous system disease, severe arthritis, pleuropericarditis or thrombopenia.There is still a doubt \u0026nbsp;regarding \u0026nbsp;tapering of the dose of IV methylprednisolone needed to achieve rapid control of activity .\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ETapering schedules are mainly based on physician’s experience and clinical judgment.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u0026nbsp;In patients requiring the therapy adequate prevention of bone loss should be applied, keeping in mind that GC-induced osteoporosis is an early event. Patients must be immunized against influenza (every year) and Streptococcus pneumoniae (every 5 years)\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ESource:\u0026nbsp;\u003Ca href=\"https:\/\/www.eular.org\/sysModules\/sysFiles\/ckeditor_4\/plugins\/doksoft_uploader\/userfiles\/18_main_CH21.docx_1.pdf\"\u003Ehttps:\/\/www.eular.org\/sysModules\/sysFiles\/ckeditor_4\/plugins\/doksoft_uploader\/userfiles\/18_main_CH21.docx_1.pdf\u003C\/a\u003E\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EAceclofenac:\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan face=\"\u0026quot;PT Sans\u0026quot;, sans-serif\" style=\"-webkit-text-size-adjust: auto; background-color: white; caret-color: rgb(102, 102, 102); color: #666666; font-size: 17px;\"\u003E“The therapeutic effect of NSAIDs is determined by the suppressed\u0026nbsp; activity of the cyclooxygenase (COX) isoenzymes COX-\u0026nbsp;1 and COX-2. The widely use of NSAIDs in clinical practice is considerably limited by the risk of adverse reactions (ARs) in the gastrointestinal\u0026nbsp;tract\u0026nbsp; (GIT), which are characteristic for this class of drugs. Medications\u0026nbsp; that are able to selectively inhibit the activity of COX-2 while\u0026nbsp; maintaining\u0026nbsp;that of COX-1 less rarely cause ARs in GIT. This selective effect is produced by aceclofenac. The drug has been also noted to be well\u0026nbsp; tolerated: the risk for aceclofenac-\u0026nbsp;induced ARs in GIT is\u0026nbsp; substantially lower than that due to the use of the majority of other NSAIDs”.\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan face=\"\u0026quot;PT Sans\u0026quot;, sans-serif\" style=\"-webkit-text-size-adjust: auto; color: #222222; font-family: sans-serif; font-size: 13.696000099182129px;\"\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\" style=\"caret-color: rgb(34, 34, 34); color: #222222; font-size: 13.696000099182129px;\"\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\" style=\"font-family: sans-serif;\"\u003E\u003Cb\u003E\u003Ci\u003Ed) Please share any \u0026nbsp;reports around similar patients with SLE and TB meningitis?\u003C\/i\u003E\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\" style=\"font-family: sans-serif;\"\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\" style=\"font-family: sans-serif;\"\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\" style=\"font-family: sans-serif;\"\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"-webkit-text-size-adjust: 100%; background-color: #fcfcfc; caret-color: rgb(51, 51, 51); color: #333333; font-family: Georgia, Palatino, serif; font-size: 18px;\"\u003ETubercular meningitis (TBM) is a rare condition in patients with systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE). The aim of this study is to describe the clinical characteristics, possible risk factors, and outcomes of SLE patients with TBM.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\" style=\"font-family: sans-serif;\"\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"-webkit-text-size-adjust: 100%; background-color: #fcfcfc; caret-color: rgb(51, 51, 51); color: #333333; font-family: Georgia, Palatino, serif; font-size: 18px;\"\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\" style=\"font-family: sans-serif;\"\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"-webkit-text-size-adjust: 100%; background-color: #fcfcfc; caret-color: rgb(51, 51, 51); color: #333333; font-family: Georgia, Palatino, serif; font-size: 18px;\"\u003EOn systematically reviewing medical records from10 SLE patients with TBM admitted to a hospital from December 2008 to December 2018. A total of 100 cases in the same period were randomly selected as controls from SLE inpatients without infection. In patients with TBM, the mean age at presentation was 35.2\u0026nbsp;years (range 19.8–45.2); the mean duration of SLE was 34.6\u0026nbsp;months (range 4–84\u0026nbsp;months). Patients with TBM had significantly longer SLE duration, higher ESR and CRP level, and lower CD4+ cell counts and albumin level than those without infections (\u003C\/span\u003E\u003Ci style=\"-webkit-text-size-adjust: 100%; box-sizing: inherit; caret-color: rgb(51, 51, 51); color: #333333; font-family: Georgia, Palatino, serif; font-size: 18px;\"\u003Ep\u003C\/i\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"-webkit-text-size-adjust: 100%; background-color: #fcfcfc; caret-color: rgb(51, 51, 51); color: #333333; font-family: Georgia, Palatino, serif; font-size: 18px;\"\u003E \u0026lt; 0.05 for all). There were no differences in prednisone dose at the time of symptom onset or cumulative dose over the preceding year between the two groups. Logistic regression analysis showed that patients with a lower CD4+ cell count were more likely to have TBM compared with controls (OR = 3.67,\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/span\u003E\u003Ci style=\"-webkit-text-size-adjust: 100%; box-sizing: inherit; caret-color: rgb(51, 51, 51); color: #333333; font-family: Georgia, Palatino, serif; font-size: 18px;\"\u003Ep\u003C\/i\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"-webkit-text-size-adjust: 100%; background-color: #fcfcfc; caret-color: rgb(51, 51, 51); color: #333333; font-family: Georgia, Palatino, serif; font-size: 18px;\"\u003E = 0.020).\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\" style=\"font-family: sans-serif;\"\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"-webkit-text-size-adjust: 100%; background-color: #fcfcfc; caret-color: rgb(51, 51, 51); color: #333333; font-family: Georgia, Palatino, serif; font-size: 18px;\"\u003ETBM should be considered when SLE patients have central nervous system (CNS) symptoms with a longer duration, higher ESR and CRP level, and lower CD4+ cell counts and albumin level, even if the patients are receiving a low prednisone dose,and the patient being studied has a chronic headache and fits into this criteria\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\" style=\"font-family: sans-serif;\"\u003E\u003Cp style=\"font-family: Helvetica; font-size: 12px; font-stretch: normal; line-height: normal; margin: 0px;\"\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp style=\"font-family: Helvetica; font-size: 12px; font-stretch: normal; line-height: normal; margin: 0px;\"\u003E\u0026nbsp;Source: https:\/\/link.springer.com\/article\/10.1007\/s10067-020-04940-9\u003C\/p\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\"\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"-webkit-text-size-adjust: 100%; background-color: #fcfcfc; caret-color: rgb(51, 51, 51); color: #333333; font-size: 18px;\"\u003E\u003Cb\u003E\u003Ci\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-family: times;\"\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/i\u003E\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\"\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\"\u003E\u003Cb\u003E\u003Ci\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-family: times;\"\u003EAny reports of normal \u0026nbsp;csf leukocyte count and normal csf protein in meningitis?\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/i\u003E\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\" style=\"font-family: sans-serif;\"\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\" style=\"font-family: sans-serif;\"\u003EWhat could be the probable cause for a normal csf leukocyte count in a patient with chronic meningitis?\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv style=\"font-family: sans-serif;\"\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\" style=\"caret-color: rgb(34, 34, 34); color: #222222; font-family: sans-serif; font-size: 13.696000099182129px;\"\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\" style=\"caret-color: rgb(34, 34, 34); color: #222222; font-size: 13.696000099182129px;\"\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\"\u003E\u003Cb\u003E\u003Ci\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-family: times;\"\u003Ee) What is the sensitivity and specificity of ANA in the diagnosis of SLE?\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/i\u003E\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cp style=\"-webkit-text-size-adjust: 100%; box-sizing: inherit; caret-color: rgb(33, 33, 33); color: #212121; font-family: BlinkMacSystemFont, -apple-system, \u0026quot;Segoe UI\u0026quot;, Roboto, Oxygen, Ubuntu, Cantarell, \u0026quot;Fira Sans\u0026quot;, \u0026quot;Droid Sans\u0026quot;, \u0026quot;Helvetica Neue\u0026quot;, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; line-height: 1.5; margin: 1.2rem 0px;\"\u003E\u003Cstrong class=\"sub-title\" style=\"box-sizing: inherit;\"\u003EMethods:\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/strong\u003ERetrospective chart review in a 400-bed teaching hospital in which\u0026nbsp;\u003Cspan style=\"background-color: white;\"\u003E1010 patients (including inpatients and outpatients) for whom ANA testing was ordered over 10 months; all patients with positive ANA test results and an equal number of randomly selected patients with negative test results were included. Clinical utility of the ANA in the identification of rheumatic disease was determined by its estimated sensitivity, specificity, and positive and negative predictive values.\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\" style=\"caret-color: rgb(34, 34, 34); color: #222222; font-family: sans-serif; font-size: 13.696000099182129px;\"\u003E\u003Cstrong class=\"sub-title\" style=\"-webkit-text-size-adjust: 100%; box-sizing: inherit; caret-color: rgb(33, 33, 33); color: #212121; font-family: BlinkMacSystemFont, -apple-system, \u0026quot;Segoe UI\u0026quot;, Roboto, Oxygen, Ubuntu, Cantarell, \u0026quot;Fira Sans\u0026quot;, \u0026quot;Droid Sans\u0026quot;, \u0026quot;Helvetica Neue\u0026quot;, sans-serif; font-size: 16px;\"\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/strong\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\" style=\"caret-color: rgb(34, 34, 34); color: #222222; font-family: sans-serif; font-size: 13.696000099182129px;\"\u003E\u003Cstrong class=\"sub-title\" style=\"-webkit-text-size-adjust: 100%; box-sizing: inherit; caret-color: rgb(33, 33, 33); color: #212121; font-family: BlinkMacSystemFont, -apple-system, \u0026quot;Segoe UI\u0026quot;, Roboto, Oxygen, Ubuntu, Cantarell, \u0026quot;Fira Sans\u0026quot;, \u0026quot;Droid Sans\u0026quot;, \u0026quot;Helvetica Neue\u0026quot;, sans-serif; font-size: 16px;\"\u003EResults:\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/strong\u003E\u003Cspan face=\"BlinkMacSystemFont, -apple-system, \u0026quot;Segoe UI\u0026quot;, Roboto, Oxygen, Ubuntu, Cantarell, \u0026quot;Fira Sans\u0026quot;, \u0026quot;Droid Sans\u0026quot;, \u0026quot;Helvetica Neue\u0026quot;, sans-serif\" style=\"-webkit-text-size-adjust: 100%; background-color: white; caret-color: rgb(33, 33, 33); color: #212121; font-size: 16px;\"\u003EOf 1010 ANA test results reviewed, 153 were positive. The group with positive ANA test results included more patients aged 65 years or older than the group with negative ANA test results (30% vs 15%, P \u0026lt; .003). The diagnosis of systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) was established in 17 patients, all of whom had positive ANA test results. Other rheumatic diseases were found in an additional 22 patients. The estimated sensitivity and specificity of the ANA test for SLE were 100% and 86%, respectively. For other rheumatic diseases, sensitivity and specificity were 42% and 85%, respectively. The positive predictive value of the ANA test was 11% for SLE and 11% for other rheumatic diseases. Specificity and positive predictive value for ANA testing in the elderly patients were lower than among younger patients\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\" style=\"caret-color: rgb(34, 34, 34); color: #222222; font-family: sans-serif; font-size: 13.696000099182129px;\"\u003E\u003Cspan face=\"BlinkMacSystemFont, -apple-system, \u0026quot;Segoe UI\u0026quot;, Roboto, Oxygen, Ubuntu, Cantarell, \u0026quot;Fira Sans\u0026quot;, \u0026quot;Droid Sans\u0026quot;, \u0026quot;Helvetica Neue\u0026quot;, sans-serif\" style=\"-webkit-text-size-adjust: 100%; background-color: white; caret-color: rgb(33, 33, 33); color: #212121; font-size: 16px;\"\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\" style=\"caret-color: rgb(34, 34, 34); color: #222222; font-family: sans-serif; font-size: 13.696000099182129px;\"\u003E\u003Cstrong class=\"sub-title\" style=\"-webkit-text-size-adjust: 100%; box-sizing: inherit; caret-color: rgb(33, 33, 33); color: #212121; font-family: BlinkMacSystemFont, -apple-system, \u0026quot;Segoe UI\u0026quot;, Roboto, Oxygen, Ubuntu, Cantarell, \u0026quot;Fira Sans\u0026quot;, \u0026quot;Droid Sans\u0026quot;, \u0026quot;Helvetica Neue\u0026quot;, sans-serif; font-size: 16px;\"\u003EConclusions:\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/strong\u003E\u003Cspan face=\"BlinkMacSystemFont, -apple-system, \u0026quot;Segoe UI\u0026quot;, Roboto, Oxygen, Ubuntu, Cantarell, \u0026quot;Fira Sans\u0026quot;, \u0026quot;Droid Sans\u0026quot;, \u0026quot;Helvetica Neue\u0026quot;, sans-serif\" style=\"-webkit-text-size-adjust: 100%; background-color: white; caret-color: rgb(33, 33, 33); color: #212121; font-size: 16px;\"\u003E\u0026nbsp;sensitivity of the ANA test for SLE was high, but overall the positive predictive value was low for SLE or other rheumatic diseases. Sensitivity was low for ANA testing among patients with non-SLE rheumatic disease. More selective test ordering might improve the clinical utility of this test. Clinicians ordering the ANA test should be aware of the test's low-positive predictive value in settings with a low prevalence of rheumatic disease, particularly among older patients.\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\" style=\"caret-color: rgb(34, 34, 34); font-size: 13.696000099182129px;\"\u003EMagnesium deficiency is associated with hypocalcemia, hypokalemia and arrhythmias and hence correlates with a higher mortality \/morbidity\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\" style=\"caret-color: rgb(34, 34, 34); font-size: 13.696000099182129px;\"\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"background-color: white;\"\u003E\u0026nbsp;If There is reduced serum magnesium they have a negative impact on glucose homeostasis and insulin sensitivity,leading to early \u0026nbsp;development of complications such as nephropathy,neuropathy and retinopathy and thus have worst outcomes compared to people who are diabetic and have normal magnesium levels.\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\" style=\"caret-color: rgb(34, 34, 34); font-size: 13.696000099182129px;\"\u003E\u003Cspan face=\"\u0026quot;Helvetica Neue\u0026quot;, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif\" style=\"-webkit-text-size-adjust: auto; background-color: white; caret-color: rgb(80, 89, 92); color: #50595c; font-size: 14px;\"\u003E“Hypomagnesemia occurs at an incidence of 13.5 to 47.7% among patients with type 2 diabetes. Poor dietary intake, autonomic dysfunction, altered insulin metabolism, glomerular hyperfiltration, osmotic diuresis, recurrent metabolic acidosis, hypophosphatemia, and hypokalemia may be contributory. Hypomagnesemia has been linked to poor glycemic control, coronary artery diseases, hypertension, diabetic retinopathy, nephropathy, neuropathy, and foot ulcerations. The increased incidence of hypomagnesemia among patients with type 2 diabetes presumably is multifactorial. Because current data suggest adverse outcomes in association with hypomagnesemia, it is prudent to monitor magnesium routinely in this patient population and treat the condition whenever possible.”\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\" style=\"caret-color: rgb(34, 34, 34); color: #222222; font-family: sans-serif; font-size: 13.696000099182129px;\"\u003E\u003Cspan face=\"\u0026quot;Helvetica Neue\u0026quot;, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif\" style=\"-webkit-text-size-adjust: auto; background-color: white; caret-color: rgb(80, 89, 92); color: #50595c; font-size: 14px;\"\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\" style=\"caret-color: rgb(34, 34, 34); color: #222222; font-family: sans-serif; font-size: 13.696000099182129px;\"\u003E\u003Cspan face=\"\u0026quot;Helvetica Neue\u0026quot;, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif\" style=\"-webkit-text-size-adjust: auto; background-color: white; caret-color: rgb(80, 89, 92); color: #50595c; font-size: 14px;\"\u003E\u0026nbsp;In addition to hyperosmolar coma and ketoacidosis, patients with type 2 diabetes may have cardiovascular disease, nephropathy, retinopathy, and polyneuropathy. With its associated complications, diabetes was reported to be the sixth leading cause of death.\u003C\/span\u003E\u003Cspan face=\"\u0026quot;Helvetica Neue\u0026quot;, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif\" style=\"-webkit-text-size-adjust: auto; background-color: white; caret-color: rgb(80, 89, 92); color: #50595c; font-size: 14px;\"\u003E\u0026nbsp;numerous studies have reported an inverse relationship between glycemic control and serum Mg levels.\u003C\/span\u003E\u003Cspan face=\"\u0026quot;Helvetica Neue\u0026quot;, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif\" style=\"-webkit-text-size-adjust: auto; background-color: white; caret-color: rgb(80, 89, 92); color: #50595c; font-size: 14px;\"\u003E\u0026nbsp;In patients with type 2 diabetes, oral Mg supplementation during a 16-wk period was suggested to improve insulin sensitivity and metabolic control\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\" style=\"caret-color: rgb(34, 34, 34); margin: 0px 0px 15px; outline: 0px; padding: 0px; vertical-align: baseline; word-wrap: break-word;\"\u003EIn a study that involved 19 normotensive individuals without diabetes, 17 hypertensive individuals without diabetes, and 6 hypertensive individuals with diabetes, Resnick\u0026nbsp;\u003Cspan style=\"-webkit-font-smoothing: antialiased; border: 0px; font-family: inherit; font-size: inherit; font-stretch: inherit; font-style: italic; font-variant-caps: inherit; line-height: inherit; margin: 0px; outline: 0px; padding: 0px; vertical-align: baseline;\"\u003Eet al.\u003C\/span\u003E\u0026nbsp;documented the lowest mean intracellular Mg concentration among the last group. Similarly, based on data from the Atherosclerosis Risk in Communities (ARIC) Study, a multicenter, prospective cohort study that lasted 4 to 7 yr and involved 13,922 middle-aged adults who were free of coronary heart disease at baseline, an inverse association between serum Mg and the risk for coronary heart disease was observed among men with diabetes\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cdiv class=\"subsection\" id=\"sec-10\" style=\"-webkit-font-smoothing: antialiased; -webkit-text-size-adjust: auto; border: 0px; caret-color: rgb(80, 89, 92); color: #50595c; font-family: \u0026quot;Helvetica Neue\u0026quot;, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif; font-size: 14px; font-stretch: inherit; line-height: inherit; margin: 0px; outline: 0px; padding: 0px; vertical-align: baseline;\"\u003E\u003Ch4 style=\"-webkit-font-smoothing: antialiased; border: 0px; color: #2c3133; font-size: 1em; font-stretch: inherit; font-style: italic; font-variant-caps: inherit; font-weight: normal; letter-spacing: 0px; line-height: 1.57em; margin: 15px 0px; outline: 0px; padding: 0px; vertical-align: baseline;\"\u003E\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/h4\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Ch4 style=\"-webkit-font-smoothing: antialiased; border: 0px; color: #2c3133; font-stretch: inherit; font-style: italic; font-weight: normal; line-height: 1.57em; margin: 15px 0px; outline: 0px; padding: 0px; vertical-align: baseline;\"\u003EDiabetic Retinopathy.\u003C\/h4\u003E\u003Cp id=\"p-10\" style=\"-webkit-font-smoothing: antialiased; border: 0px; font-stretch: inherit; line-height: inherit; margin: 0px 0px 15px; outline: 0px; padding: 0px; vertical-align: baseline; word-wrap: break-word;\"\u003EThe link between hypomagnesemia and diabetic retinopathy was reported in two cross-sectional studies that involved both “insulin-dependent” patients and patients with type 2 diabetes. Not only did patients with diabetes have lower serum Mg levels compared with their counterparts without diabetes, but also the\u0026nbsp;\u003Cb\u003Eserum Mg levels among the cohort with diabetes had an inverse correlation with the degree of retinopathy\u003C\/b\u003E\u0026nbsp;.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp id=\"p-10\" style=\"-webkit-font-smoothing: antialiased; word-wrap: break-word;\"\u003EIn a comparative study that involved 30 patients who had type 2 diabetes without microalbuminuria, 30 with microalbuminuria, and 30 with overt proteinuria, Corsonello\u0026nbsp;\u003Cspan style=\"-webkit-font-smoothing: antialiased; color: #222222; font-family: sans-serif; font-size: 13.696000099182129px;\"\u003EWhat is the current available evidence for the utility of monitoring salt excretion in the hypertensive population?\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003C\/div\u003EHigh dietary intake of sodium is seen in most of the subjects who have very high blood pressures\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\" style=\"caret-color: rgb(34, 34, 34);\"\u003EBy the means of a self monitoring device\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\" style=\"caret-color: rgb(34, 34, 34);\"\u003E\u003Cspan face=\"BlinkMacSystemFont, -apple-system, \u0026quot;Segoe UI\u0026quot;, Roboto, Oxygen, Ubuntu, Cantarell, \u0026quot;Fira Sans\u0026quot;, \u0026quot;Droid Sans\u0026quot;, \u0026quot;Helvetica Neue\u0026quot;, sans-serif\" style=\"-webkit-text-size-adjust: 100%; background-color: white; caret-color: rgb(33, 33, 33); color: #212121; font-size: 16px;\"\u003ESubjects were 34 hypertensive patients who underwent successful 24-h home urine collection five times and 25 volunteers. Four volunteers were diagnosed as having hypertension based on home blood pressure (BP) readings. All subjects were asked to measure daily urinary salt excretion for 30 days by using a self-monitoring device which estimates 24-h salt excretion by overnight urine. The mean urinary salt excretion during the 30 days was 8.36 +\/- 1.52 g\/day and the range (maximum-minimum value) was 5.47 +\/- 20.05 g\/day in all subjects. Mean urinary salt excretion decreased from 8.52 +\/- 1.63 g\/day for the first 10 days to 8.31 +\/- 1.54 g\/day for the last 10 days (p \u0026lt; 0.05). The mean urinary salt excretion determined by a self-monitoring device using overnight urine was positively associated with that determined by 24-h home urine for five times in the hypertensive subjects (r = 0.63, p \u0026lt; 0.01). \u003Cb\u003EResults indicate that a self-monitoring device seems to be useful to monitor daily salt intake and to guide salt restriction.\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv dir=\"auto\" style=\"caret-color: rgb(34, 34, 34);\"\u003E\u003Cspan face=\"BlinkMacSystemFont, -apple-system, \u0026quot;Segoe UI\u0026quot;, Roboto, Oxygen, Ubuntu, Cantarell, \u0026quot;Fira Sans\u0026quot;, \u0026quot;Droid Sans\u0026quot;, \u0026quot;Helvetica Neue\u0026quot;, sans-serif\" style=\"-webkit-text-size-adjust: 100%;
